function: above_phy (p. 7): the PPO agent learns UAV placement, the AR rendering/offloading split, and block-producer selection; bandwidth and computing allocation use a non-learned Lagrangian method (p. 8).
notes: Excluded at Step 1, check 4 (above_phy). Check 3 (no_learning) does not apply because a learned PPO-based DRL agent is the primary routine of the method, but it acts above the physical layer. p. 7: "To solve the URBS problem, the PPO algorithm is adopted", where URBS is the "UAV development, rendering decision, and block producer selection"; p. 7: "The action space in the system comprises three primary elements, i.e., the UAV location, the block producer decision, and the rendering decision." The rendering decision is a task-offloading/edge-computing split (p. 5: "the proportion of the original AR tasks that UAV m needs to process"), UAV location is UAV placement, and block-producer selection is blockchain consensus management. The only physical-layer-like decision, the OFDMA bandwidth allocation of the UAV-to-user downlink, is not learned: p. 7: "For the CBRA problem, we design a Lagrangian Multiplier Iterative (LMI)-based algorithm"; p. 8, Algorithm 1: "Calculate bm,um by using Newton’s method". So the aerial-link exception (learned resource allocation counts as physical layer) does not apply. Although p. 7 says the DRL "can learn the optimal CBRA strategy from the environment", bandwidth and CPU frequencies are not in the action space; the LMI solver is embedded in the DRL environment. Tables I (p. 4) and II (p. 10), read from the page images, show no learned physical-layer decision. Page 1 holds the title "Blockchain-Based AR Offloading in UAV-Enabled MEC Networks: A Trade-Off Between Energy Consumption and Rendering Latency" and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3581015, so the PDF matches the DOI.
